_comment: Stand-in data for the admin view. NOT from the cluster.
The admin view's job is to show a judge how the agents work. Parts of that
machinery do not record themselves yet, and this file supplies those in the
exact shape the real source will return — so wiring it up later means
filling the block and changing 'source' from 'placeholder' to 'live', with
no key moving and no renderer changing.
Rules enforced by build_web.merge_placeholders, not by convention:
1. Every block must declare a 'source'. The page badges it from there.
2. No block may name a guarded key (runs, finds, summary, months,
ratings, kinds, corpus, or the find id lists). Those are the rows the
page presents as the cluster's own.
3. No block may carry a money value, as a field or quoted in prose.
Placeholders may state how the machinery ran; they may never state
what it earned. This is why the answers below count finds instead of
dollars, and it is checked, not trusted.
WHAT IS HERE, AND WHY IT IS NOT REAL YET
ask.sessions -- The Ask agent answers a question by running read-only SQL
against the live cluster over CockroachDB's managed MCP server. Its run
already stores the SQL trail in agent_run.note, and build_web reads it
back (see ask_sessions) -- so runId, askedAt, seconds, trail and
queriedTheCluster all become real the moment one Ask run exists in the
export. The seeded cluster has never run Ask, which is why the list is
empty without this file.
The two fields that are NOT merely unpopulated but unstorable are
'question' and 'answer': agent_run has no column for either. Making those
real needs a schema change, and that is tracked as follow-up rather than
papered over here.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE
Token counts. agent_run has input_tokens/output_tokens columns and
nothing in the codebase ever writes them, so the page reports them as
unrecorded. A stand-in number would claim instrumentation we do not have.
The retrieval funnel's dedup stage. The Analyst writes its retrieved
count into its own run note, so it becomes real with no schema change as
soon as an analyst run is exported. Until then the page shows it as not
recorded, which is a truer thing to show a judge than a plausible number.

sessions.question: Which of the moves we shipped actually beat what the agent predicted?
sessions.answer: Six of the seven judged moves came in at or above their prediction. One missed: the espresso upsell after dessert measured no lift at all, and it is the only find in the ledger carrying a miss.
trail: select_query SELECT f.title, le.verdict, le.measured_at FROM ledger_entry le JOIN find f ON f.id = le.find_id WHERE le.business_id = '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111' ORDER BY le.measured_at DESC
select_query SELECT verdict, count(*) FROM ledger_entry WHERE business_id = '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111' GROUP BY verdict

sessions.question: What did the agent read before it told me to raise the pasta mains?
sessions.answer: Nine observations, every one of them retrieved by vector search and stored against that find. The closest, at 0.743 cosine similarity, was a rival putting two dollars on its own pasta mains across the board this month.
trail: select_query [FAILED] SELECT * FROM evidence WHERE find_id = 'e9b685b5'
select_query SELECT o.content, o.kind, fe.similarity, fe.rank FROM find_evidence fe JOIN observation o ON o.id = fe.observation_id WHERE fe.find_id = 'e9b685b5' ORDER BY fe.rank

sessions.question: What is a good margin for an Italian restaurant?
sessions.answer: That is a general question rather than one about this business, so nothing was read from the cluster. Ask about the finds, the observations behind them, or the ledger and the agent will query the database.
